bio.text: Rinaldi Anwar Buyung isn't just an actuary; he's a tech entrepreneur actively architecting the future of insurance. He is the Founder of Seleris, a cutting-edge SaaS platform that leverages the power of Artificial Intelligence to revolutionize the underwriting process.

Seleris is the direct application of his deep academic work as a Doctoral researcher in AI and Data Science. His vision is backed by a prolific research portfolio, including dozens of scientific journals on AI technology, proving he's not just part of the conversation—he's driving it.
With 30 years of industry-experience, Rinaldi possesses a rare blend of deep technical mastery in mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, underwriting, and risk management.

He remains a dynamic force in the industry, actively pioneering new innovations at the intersection of healthcare, insurance, and finance. He serves as a high-level strategic advisor and holds senior governance roles across the insurance, reinsurance, and risk consulting sectors. As an actuary, Rinaldi is a central figure who both understands the industry's foundations and is actively building its future.

sci.title: Capturing Facial Blood Flow Video
sci.body: Captures real-time facial video to analyze micro blood flow changes using standard cameras. This process is non-contact and helps extract physiological signals from skin color fluctuations linked to blood circulation.

sci.title: Object Detection
sci.body: Detects and tracks facial areas and other relevant objects to ensure the correct region is monitored throughout the video. This improves accuracy by isolating key visual components.

sci.title: Requirement Condition Detection
sci.body: Automatically checks for environmental and positional requirements such as lighting quality, subject distance, and motion artifacts. This ensures the system only processes usable and reliable visual data.

sci.title: Region of Interest (ROI)
sci.body: Selects specific facial zones (like the forehead or cheeks) where blood flow signals are most visible. Focusing on ROI improves signal strength and reduces noise from unrelated areas.

sci.title: Raw (RGB) Signals Extraction
sci.body: Extracts color channel values (Red, Green, Blue) from the ROI. These raw signals form the basis for further physiological analysis, capturing subtle changes caused by blood flow variations.

sdv.title: rPPG Signals Extraction
sdv.body: Derives remote photoplethysmographic (rPPG) signals from facial video data. These signals reflect vital signs such as heart rate and are extracted without physical sensors.

sdv.title: Signal Filtering
sdv.body: Applies advanced signal processing filters to enhance relevant health data while removing interference. This step ensures the extracted rPPG signals are clean and ready for analysis.

sdv.title: Noise Reduction
sdv.body: Removes unwanted disturbances like lighting changes or small head movements from the signal. This enhances the clarity of health indicators by eliminating signal artifacts.

sdv.title: AI Feature Extraction
sdv.body: Uses machine learning algorithms to identify critical patterns in the cleaned signals. The system recognizes features such as heart rate variability and other biometric indicators.

sdv.title: Feature Prediction
sdv.body: Predicts key physiological parameters based on the extracted features, such as estimated pulse, respiration rate, and stress indicators enabling fast, contactless health insights.

sdr.title: Health Risk Scoring
sdr.body: Generates a quantifiable score based on physiological input to assess an individual's current health condition. This score helps users and providers make informed wellness or diagnostic decisions.

sdr.title: Underwriting Risk Prediction
sdr.body: Predicts insurance underwriting risks by analyzing biometric data. It provides insurers with automated risk profiling to accelerate and improve decision-making accuracy.

sdr.title: Risk Diseases Prediction
sdr.body: Assesses the likelihood of chronic or critical diseases by combining physiological indicators with AI modeling. It aids early detection and targeted interventions.

sdr.title: Mortality/Morbidity Risk Prediction
sdr.body: Estimates potential health deterioration or death risk using biometric and behavioral data. This insight supports healthcare, insurance, and wellness decision-making for long-term planning.

metrics.title: Heart Rate
metrics.description: Heart rate indicates how many times your heart beats per minute. Normal resting range is 60–100 bpm.

metrics.title: Heart Rate Variability
metrics.description: HRV measures the variation in time between heartbeats. Higher HRV generally indicates better cardiovascular fitness.

metrics.title: Breath Rate
metrics.description: Respiratory rate is the number of breaths taken per minute. Normal range is 12–20 brpm.

metrics.title: Systolic Pressure
metrics.description: Systolic pressure measures the force of blood against artery walls when the heart beats.

metrics.title: Diastolic Pressure
metrics.description: Diastolic pressure measures artery pressure when the heart is resting between beats.

scanSdk.cameraUnavailable: This device reports no usable camera, so the scan cannot start.
scanSdk.heatmapWaiting: The heatmap is not ready to save yet.
scanSdk.helpPermission: Camera access was blocked. Open the lock icon in the address bar, allow the camera, then try again.
scanSdk.helpCameraBusy: Pick an available camera and close any other app or tab that is using it, then try again.
scanSdk.helpPreflight: The camera delivered frames too slowly during the 3-second check — it needs about 24 per second. Close DevTools first (it slows the scanner the most), use brighter light from the front, close other tabs and apps using the CPU or camera, and turn off the perfusion heatmap.
scanSdk.retryNoHeatmap: Turn off heatmap and try again
scanSdk.helpPreflightAccepted: Frames arrived fast enough, but too many were rejected. Take off glasses, sunglasses or a mask — they block admission. Light your face from the front, fill the frame with one face, and hold still.
scanSdk.accessoryBlocking: Detected on your face: {item}. Glasses, sunglasses and masks block the scan. Please take it off and try again.
scanSdk.fpsEmpty: No readings yet. Start a scan to record the frame rate.
scanSdk.fpsCopy: Copy report for the SDK team
scanSdk.fpsCopyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text above manually.
scanSdk.errorTitle: The scan could not be completed

check.ready: Camera ready — {hz} frames per second, lighting is good.
check.tooSlow: Your camera only delivers {hz} frames per second. The scan needs {need}.
check.tooSlowHelp: Almost always the light: in a dim room the camera slows itself down to brighten the picture. Face a window or a lamp, close other apps using the camera, and plug the laptop into power.
check.tooDark: Not enough light on your face.
check.tooDarkHelp: Light your face from the front. A window or lamp behind the screen works well. Scanning in this light will likely be rejected.
check.backlightHelp: Your background is brighter than your face, so the camera darkens you. Turn around, or close the curtain behind you.

scanSdk.helpCameraCadence: This camera cannot deliver {hz} frames per second, which the scan requires. Brighter light from the front usually fixes it — in dim rooms the camera slows itself down. Otherwise pick a different camera or device.
scanSdk.helpMotionLip: The scan was stopped because your mouth kept moving. Please do not talk or chew during the 30 seconds — hold a neutral expression.
scanSdk.helpMotionPose: The scan was stopped because your head kept turning. Face the camera straight on and keep your head in one position.
scanSdk.helpMotionScale: The scan was stopped because the distance to the camera kept changing. Sit back, keep the same distance, and avoid leaning in or out.
scanSdk.helpMotion: The scan was stopped because your face moved too much. Rest your back against the chair, hold your head still, and try again.
scanSdk.notIsolated: This page is not cross-origin isolated, so the scanner runs single-threaded and may struggle to reach the required frame rate.
